title: DELL — Dell Technologies
html:
Close: $461.56 · Day: +1.5% · Week: −19.3% · YTD: +270% Trend: long-term uptrend still intact (well above the 200-day at $316.43), but it broke below the 20-day ($536.24) and 50-day ($512.67). RSI(14): 36 · ATR(14): about $31 a day (~7%) · Volatility: ~59% annualized. A very fast-moving stock.

Story: an AI-server winner. Revenue grew 58% last quarter, and its AI infrastructure unit is now over half of sales. On Oct 14 Barclays downgraded it to Equal Weight over worries that companies are adopting AI more slowly. The stock fell 11.3% that day and kept sliding with the chip selloff (Trefis).

The levels that matter

  • Right now: today it dipped to $439.50, under the 38.2% of the recent swing ($454.07), then closed back above it. That's a possible reversal sign, but one day isn't confirmation.
  • Support — strong cluster: $409–411, where the 38.2% of the big swing ($409.36) meets the 50% of the recent swing ($410.63).
  • Resistance: $480 (lost Fib level), then $507.81, then the 50-day at ~$513.

Earnings: around Nov 23, 2026 (not yet confirmed).

Edge study caution: buying DELL's dips has not worked historically. The uptrend + RSI<40 setup (flashing now) won only 50% of the time over 20 days, and Fib pullbacks won just 36%. DELL's big gains came from riding its trend, not from buying its dips. With a $31 daily range, any options position here needs very small size.
